one_month_reasoning: The key event in the window is Q3 2026 results, expected around Oct 27, 2026 (NXP released Q3 2025 on Oct 27/28, 2025 per EDGAR 8-K item 2.02 dated 2025-10-28; Q2 2026 came out July 28), so it lands before the Oct 29 scoring close. Q3 guide was $3.75B revenue (+7% q/q) and $4.11 EPS at the midpoint. Management said in July and again at Goldman Sachs on Sep 9 that momentum carries into Q4, lead times are getting longer, and price increases build through Q3/Q4. A beat is likely because NXP has cleared the guidance midpoint in recent quarters. But the reaction depends on the Q4 guide versus consensus (~$4.3 EPS implied by the $15.06 FY26 consensus), and the Q2 beat still sold off 7-15%. Net: a small positive tilt to the median (~$238), with the monthly sigma set at about 13.5%, near 48%/3.5, because the earnings event pushes out both tails. The Oct 8 dividend is paid after the Sep 16 record date, so it has no ex-date effect in the window.

fair_value.method: Blend of forward P/E (60%): NTM EPS at Sep-2027 of $19.0 x 15x = $285; and FCF yield (40%): 2027 FCF/share $15.2 at a 5.75% yield = $264. Blended ~$277, rounded to $275.

inputs_detail.derivation: FY27 consensus $18.13 grown ~10% into 2028 (matching management's 2030 goal of doubling EPS from $11.81, a ~15% CAGR, and the 34-40% operating margin target), giving a Q4'27-Q3'28 run-rate of ~$19.8. Haircut ~4% for peak-cycle pricing and China pull-in risk (China revenue +31.5% q/q in Q2) -> $19.0

The stock is ~13.3x NTM consensus today ($236.47 / ~$17.7) and was ~19x in June at $300 (TIKR). 15x sits between the two: some re-rating as margins reach the 2027 targets, but not the June peak multiple, because the market now treats NXP's earnings as near cycle highs

methods.name: FCF yield
methods.inputs: 2027 revenue $15.88B x 24% FCF margin = $3.81B / ~250M shares = $15.2 FCF/share, capitalized at 5.75%

inputs_detail.derivation: Q2 2026 FCF margin 22.6% and FY2025 19.8%. Capex runs ~2-3% of revenue, but VSMC/ESMC JV capacity fees and equity injections continue (Q3: $70M fees + $80M VSMC + $30M ESMC). With operating leverage at higher revenue, 24% is plausible
252.2M shares outstanding on July 24, 2026 and 254M diluted in the Q3 guide. Buybacks slowed ($104M in Q2), so assume only ~1% net reduction

At $236.47 the 2027 FCF yield is ~6.4%. At the $300 June price it was ~5.1%. 5.75% is the midpoint, which reflects cyclicality and ~$7.75B of net debt (Q2 balance sheet: $999M short-term + $9,977M long-term debt - $3,222M cash; net leverage 1.5x)

bear.story: The auto/industrial upturn stalls in 2027. The China surge (+31.5% q/q in Q2) and distributor strength prove partly pull-in, price increases reverse, and Chinese competitors keep taking MCU/ADAS/IVI share. FY27 EPS comes in ~$15 rather than $18, and the stock trades at ~11x NTM, near its March 2026 trough multiple.

base.story: NXP delivers roughly consensus: 2026 EPS ~$15, 2027 ~$18. Gross margin moves toward 59-60%, data center passes $500M, and the SDV/physical-AI ramps begin in late 2027. The multiple recovers only partly, to ~14x a ~$19 NTM EPS, because investors stay wary of peak-cycle earnings.

bull.story: The pricing reset sticks and lead times keep extending. Revenue beats the 2027 plan and gross margin reaches the 60%+ target, with NTM EPS ~$21. The market re-rates NXP toward the 17-18x it held in May-June 2026, retesting the $340 high and going beyond it.

thesis_break_reason: $175 is below the 52-week low ($183) and implies only ~9.5-10x NTM consensus EPS. At that level the market would be discounting an earnings reset (FY27 EPS nearer $14-15 than $18), for example a guide-down showing that 2026 demand was pull-in or restocking, lost pricing, or a China/export-control shock. That would contradict management's repeated no-restocking and lean-inventory statements. The drawdown from May to August ($340 to $229) happened with fundamentals still rising, so moves in the $200-230 range are ordinary volatility for this stock.

reasoning: The primary documents show fundamentals accelerating while the stock derated. Q2 2026 revenue was $3.50B (+19% y/y), non-GAAP GM 58.0%, OM 35.1% and EPS $3.61. The Q3 guide is $3.75B / $4.11 EPS with GM 58.5%, and channel inventory is steady at 11 weeks. The 10-Q adds detail the recaps skip: China revenue rose 31.5% q/q and distributor sales 11.3% q/q. Management says there is no restocking, but I treat this as the main pull-in risk. The Sep 9 Goldman Sachs remarks said price increases build into 2027 and lead times are lengthening. Shares still fell from $340 (May) to $229 (end of July) and now sit at ~13x NTM consensus EPS (~$17.7), with FY27 consensus at $18.13. My fair value of ~$275 blends 15x NTM Sep-2027 EPS of $19 ($285) with a 5.75% FCF yield on $15.2 of 2027 FCF/share ($264). The scenario-weighted mean is ~$265. I put the distribution median lower, at ~$256, because of the negative skew of cyclical earnings and weak momentum. The ladder is lognormal around that median with a 44% sigma, a little below the 48% realized volatility, which was inflated by the Apr-May spike. That gives P(>=spot) ~57%, and the bear/bull tails match the scenario prices ($170 / $360). Research was limited: Twelve Data and Alpha Vantage estimate endpoints were unavailable, so consensus comes from stockanalysis.com.
